top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 142, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)'s mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)'s demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu). Train it until it feels boring.
At Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu), surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)'s mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 142 miles.
142 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 142 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)'s mixed terrain actually does to you.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 142 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Tempo is Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)'s race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 142 miles on mixed terrain. Train it until it's automatic.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Estonia (Tallinn-Tartu)’s 142 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, TT Threshold, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 142 miles of mixed terrain in Tallinn to Tartu, Estonia (point-to-point).
